def _check_targets(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """For classification, check that the targets `y` match the logits `f`
    `(batch, ..., classes)`: class indices `(batch, ...)` or class probabilities
    with the same shape as `f`.

    Flattening the batch dims would silently misalign targets of the wrong shape
    with the same number of elements, e.g. `(B, L, M)` instead of `(B, M, L)`.
    """
    if self.likelihood != Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION:
        return

    if y.shape != f.shape[:-1] and y.shape != f.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The targets have shape {tuple(y.shape)}, which matches neither the "
            f"class indices {tuple(f.shape[:-1])} nor the class probabilities "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)} expected from the logits."
        )

def _loss(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute `self.lossfunc(f, y)`, where every leading dim of `f` but the last
    is a batch dim.

    `CrossEntropyLoss` expects the class axis at dim 1, while Laplace puts it last,
    e.g. logits `(B, L, C)` with targets `(B, L)`. So, for classification, flatten
    the batch dims, which makes every token an observation.
    """
    self._check_targets(f, y)

    if self.likelihood == Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION and f.ndim > 2:
        # Class probabilities keep their class axis
        y = y.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1]) if y.ndim == f.ndim else y.reshape(-1)
        f = f.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1])

    return self.lossfunc(f, y)

Parameters:

    input data (batch, input_shape) on compatible device with model if torch.Tensor. If MutableMapping, then at least contains self.dict_key_x. The latter is specific for reward modeling.

    whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_\\theta f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using asdfghjkl's gradient per output dimension.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping (e.g. dict, UserDict)
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model if torch.Tensor.
        If MutableMapping, then at least contains `self.dict_key_x`.
        The latter is specific for reward modeling.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `([batch_dims], outputs, parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `([batch_dims], outputs)`
    """
    Js = list()
    # `self.model.output_size` can be stale, e.g. in reward modeling where the
    # output size differs between fitting and prediction. So, get the number of
    # outputs from the first forward pass instead.
    n_outputs = 1
    i = 0
    while i < n_outputs:

        def closure():
            self.model.zero_grad()
            f = self.model(x)
            loss = f[..., i].sum()
            loss.backward(
                create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
            )
            return f

        Ji, f = self._batch_gradient(closure)
        n_outputs = f.shape[-1]

        if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
            Ji = Ji[:, self.subnetwork_indices]

        Js.append(Ji)
        i += 1

    Js = torch.stack(Js, dim=1)  # (n_rows, n_outputs, n_params)

    # ASDL returns one row per row of the layers' inputs, e.g. per token. Sum those
    # belonging to the same observation, e.g. when the outputs are pooled over tokens.
    n_obs = f.shape[:-1].numel()
    Js = self._sum_rows_per_observation(Js, n_obs)

    if Js.shape[0] == n_obs:
        # Restore the individual batch dims of the outputs
        Js = Js.reshape(*f.shape[:-1], *Js.shape[-2:])

    return Js, f

def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def _check_targets(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """For classification, check that the targets `y` match the logits `f`
    `(batch, ..., classes)`: class indices `(batch, ...)` or class probabilities
    with the same shape as `f`.

    Flattening the batch dims would silently misalign targets of the wrong shape
    with the same number of elements, e.g. `(B, L, M)` instead of `(B, M, L)`.
    """
    if self.likelihood != Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION:
        return

    if y.shape != f.shape[:-1] and y.shape != f.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The targets have shape {tuple(y.shape)}, which matches neither the "
            f"class indices {tuple(f.shape[:-1])} nor the class probabilities "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)} expected from the logits."
        )

def _loss(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute `self.lossfunc(f, y)`, where every leading dim of `f` but the last
    is a batch dim.

    `CrossEntropyLoss` expects the class axis at dim 1, while Laplace puts it last,
    e.g. logits `(B, L, C)` with targets `(B, L)`. So, for classification, flatten
    the batch dims, which makes every token an observation.
    """
    self._check_targets(f, y)

    if self.likelihood == Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION and f.ndim > 2:
        # Class probabilities keep their class axis
        y = y.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1]) if y.ndim == f.ndim else y.reshape(-1)
        f = f.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1])

    return self.lossfunc(f, y)

def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

Parameters:

def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using backpack's BatchGrad per output dimension. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, parameters, outputs)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    model = extend(self.model)
    to_stack = []
    for i in range(model.output_size):
        model.zero_grad()
        out = model(x)
        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            if model.output_size > 1:
                out[:, i].sum().backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
            else:
                out.sum().backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
            to_cat = []
            for param in model.parameters():
                to_cat.append(param.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1))
                delattr(param, "grad_batch")
            Jk = torch.cat(to_cat, dim=1)
            if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
                Jk = Jk[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
        to_stack.append(Jk)
        if i == 0:
            f = out

    model.zero_grad()
    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad
    CTX.remove_hooks()
    _cleanup(model)
    if model.output_size > 1:
        J = torch.stack(to_stack, dim=2).transpose(1, 2)
    else:
        J = Jk.unsqueeze(-1).transpose(1, 2)

    return (J, f) if enable_backprop else (J.detach(), f.detach())

def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at current parameter
    \\(\\theta\\) using Backpack's BatchGrad. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    y : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(batch, parameters)`
    loss : torch.Tensor
    """
    f = self.model(x)
    loss = self.lossfunc(f, y)
    with backpack(BatchGrad()):
        loss.backward()
    Gs = torch.cat(
        [p.grad_batch.data.flatten(start_dim=1) for p in self._model.parameters()],
        dim=1,
    )
    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
    return Gs, loss

  • outputs (Tensor) –

    Output indices for each input, shaped (batch,) or (batch, selected_outputs).

  • enable_backprop (bool, default: False ) –

    Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

Returns:

def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute selected output Jacobians using BackPACK's BatchGrad.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        Input data of shape `(batch, input_shape)` on the model's device.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != x.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    model = extend(self.model)
    columns = []
    first_output = None

    for column in range(outputs.shape[1]):
        model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        output = model(x)
        if first_output is None:
            first_output = output

        selected = output.gather(
            1, outputs[:, column : column + 1].to(output.device)
        ).sum()

        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            selected.backward(
                create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
            )
            columns.append(
                torch.cat(
                    [
                        parameter.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
                        for parameter in model.parameters()
                        if parameter.requires_grad
                    ],
                    dim=1,
                )
            )
            for parameter in model.parameters():
                if hasattr(parameter, "grad_batch"):
                    delattr(parameter, "grad_batch")

    model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad
    CTX.remove_hooks()
    _cleanup(model)

    result = torch.stack(columns, dim=1)
    assert first_output is not None

    return (
        (result, first_output)
        if enable_backprop
        else (
            result.detach(),
            first_output.detach(),
        )
    )

        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute selected output Jacobians using BackPACK's BatchGrad.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        Input data of shape `(batch, input_shape)` on the model's device.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != x.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    model = extend(self.model)
    columns = []
    first_output = None

    for column in range(outputs.shape[1]):
        model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        output = model(x)
        if first_output is None:
            first_output = output

        selected = output.gather(
            1, outputs[:, column : column + 1].to(output.device)
        ).sum()

        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            selected.backward(
                create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
            )
            columns.append(
                torch.cat(
                    [
                        parameter.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
                        for parameter in model.parameters()
                        if parameter.requires_grad
                    ],
                    dim=1,
                )
            )
            for parameter in model.parameters():
                if hasattr(parameter, "grad_batch"):
                    delattr(parameter, "grad_batch")

    model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad
    CTX.remove_hooks()
    _cleanup(model)

    result = torch.stack(columns, dim=1)
    assert first_output is not None

    return (
        (result, first_output)
        if enable_backprop
        else (
            result.detach(),
            first_output.detach(),
        )
    )

def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at current parameter
    \\(\\theta\\) using Backpack's BatchGrad. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    -------

    return Gs, loss

Compute the full GGN \(P \times P\) matrix as Hessian approximation \(H_{ggn}\) with respect to parameters \(\theta \in \mathbb{R}^P\). For last-layer, reduced to \(\theta_{last}\)

Parameters:

  • x (Tensor) –

  • y (Tensor) –

Returns:

Source code in laplace/curvature/curvature.py 
def full(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the full GGN \\(P \\times P\\) matrix as Hessian approximation
    \\(H_{ggn}\\) with respect to parameters \\(\\theta \\in \\mathbb{R}^P\\).
    For last-layer, reduced to \\(\\theta_{last}\\)

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)`
    y : torch.Tensor
        labels `(batch, label_shape)`

    Returns
    -------
    loss : torch.Tensor
    H : torch.Tensor
        GGN `(parameters, parameters)`
    """
    Js, f = self.last_layer_jacobians(x) if self.last_layer else self.jacobians(x)
    H_lik = (
        self._get_mc_functional_fisher(f)
        if self.stochastic
        else self._get_functional_hessian(f)
    )

    if H_lik is not None:
        H = torch.einsum("...cp,...ck,...kq->pq", Js, H_lik, Js)
    else:  # The case of exact GGN for regression
        H = torch.einsum("...cp,...cq->pq", Js, Js)
    loss = self.factor * self._loss(f, y)

    return loss.detach(), H.detach()

docs.text:
_get_mc_functional_fisher(f: Tensor) -> Tensor

Approximate the Fisher's middle matrix (expected outer product of the functional gradient) using MC integral with self.num_samples many samples.

Source code in laplace/curvature/curvature.py 
def _get_mc_functional_fisher(self, f: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Approximate the Fisher's middle matrix (expected outer product of the functional gradient)
    using MC integral with `self.num_samples` many samples.
    """
    F = 0

    for _ in range(self.num_samples):
        if self.likelihood == "regression":
            # N(y | f, 1)
            y_sample = f + torch.randn(f.shape, device=f.device, dtype=f.dtype)
            grad_sample = f - y_sample  # functional MSE grad
        else:  # classification with softmax
            y_sample = torch.distributions.Multinomial(logits=f).sample()
            # First functional derivative of the loglik is p - y
            p = torch.softmax(f, dim=-1)
            grad_sample = p - y_sample

        F += (
            1
            / self.num_samples
            * torch.einsum("...c,...k->...ck", grad_sample, grad_sample)
        )

    return F

def _check_targets(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """For classification, check that the targets `y` match the logits `f`
    `(batch, ..., classes)`: class indices `(batch, ...)` or class probabilities
    with the same shape as `f`.

    Flattening the batch dims would silently misalign targets of the wrong shape
    with the same number of elements, e.g. `(B, L, M)` instead of `(B, M, L)`.
    """
    if self.likelihood != Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION:
        return

    if y.shape != f.shape[:-1] and y.shape != f.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The targets have shape {tuple(y.shape)}, which matches neither the "
            f"class indices {tuple(f.shape[:-1])} nor the class probabilities "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)} expected from the logits."
        )

Compute self.lossfunc(f, y), where every leading dim of f but the last is a batch dim.

CrossEntropyLoss expects the class axis at dim 1, while Laplace puts it last, e.g. logits (B, L, C) with targets (B, L). So, for classification, flatten the batch dims, which makes every token an observation.

def _loss(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute `self.lossfunc(f, y)`, where every leading dim of `f` but the last
    is a batch dim.

    `CrossEntropyLoss` expects the class axis at dim 1, while Laplace puts it last,
    e.g. logits `(B, L, C)` with targets `(B, L)`. So, for classification, flatten
    the batch dims, which makes every token an observation.
    """
    self._check_targets(f, y)

    if self.likelihood == Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION and f.ndim > 2:
        # Class probabilities keep their class axis
        y = y.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1]) if y.ndim == f.ndim else y.reshape(-1)
        f = f.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1])

    return self.lossfunc(f, y)

Parameters:

def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\)
    using backpack's BatchGrad per output dimension. Note that BackPACK doesn't play well
    with torch.func, so this method has to be overridden.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, parameters, outputs)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        raise ValueError("BackPACK backend does not support dict-like inputs!")

    input_grad = (
        x.grad.detach().clone() if x.is_leaf and x.grad is not None else None
    )
    model = extend(self.model)
    to_stack = []
    for i in range(model.output_size):
        model.zero_grad()
        out = model(x)
        with backpack(BatchGrad()):
            if model.output_size > 1:
                out[:, i].sum().backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
            else:
                out.sum().backward(
                    create_graph=enable_backprop, retain_graph=enable_backprop
                )
            to_cat = []
            for param in model.parameters():
                to_cat.append(param.grad_batch.reshape(x.shape[0], -1))
                delattr(param, "grad_batch")
            Jk = torch.cat(to_cat, dim=1)
            if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
                Jk = Jk[:, self.subnetwork_indices]
        to_stack.append(Jk)
        if i == 0:
            f = out

    model.zero_grad()
    if x.is_leaf and x.requires_grad:
        x.grad = input_grad
    CTX.remove_hooks()
    _cleanup(model)
    if model.output_size > 1:
        J = torch.stack(to_stack, dim=2).transpose(1, 2)
    else:
        J = Jk.unsqueeze(-1).transpose(1, 2)

    return (J, f) if enable_backprop else (J.detach(), f.detach())

def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def full(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    y: torch.Tensor,
    **kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the full EF \\(P \\times P\\) matrix as Hessian approximation
    \\(H_{ef}\\) with respect to parameters \\(\\theta \\in \\mathbb{R}^P\\).
    For last-layer, reduced to \\(\\theta_{last}\\)

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)`
    y : torch.Tensor
        labels `(batch, label_shape)`

    Returns
    -------
    loss : torch.Tensor
    H_ef : torch.Tensor
        EF `(parameters, parameters)`
    """
    Gs, loss = self.gradients(x, y)
    Gs, loss = Gs.detach(), loss.detach()
    H_ef = torch.einsum("bp,bq->pq", Gs, Gs)
    return self.factor * loss.detach(), self.factor * H_ef

    with the same number of elements, e.g. `(B, L, M)` instead of `(B, M, L)`.
    """
    if self.likelihood != Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION:
        return

    if y.shape != f.shape[:-1] and y.shape != f.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The targets have shape {tuple(y.shape)}, which matches neither the "
            f"class indices {tuple(f.shape[:-1])} nor the class probabilities "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)} expected from the logits."

def _loss(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute `self.lossfunc(f, y)`, where every leading dim of `f` but the last
    is a batch dim.

    `CrossEntropyLoss` expects the class axis at dim 1, while Laplace puts it last,
    e.g. logits `(B, L, C)` with targets `(B, L)`. So, for classification, flatten
    the batch dims, which makes every token an observation.
    """
    self._check_targets(f, y)

    if self.likelihood == Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION and f.ndim > 2:
        # Class probabilities keep their class axis
        y = y.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1]) if y.ndim == f.ndim else y.reshape(-1)
        f = f.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1])

    return self.lossfunc(f, y)

def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\),
    via torch.func.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `([batch_dims], outputs, parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `([batch_dims], outputs)`
    """

    def model_fn_params_only(params_dict, buffers_dict):
        out = torch.func.functional_call(self.model, (params_dict, buffers_dict), x)
        return out, out

    Js, f = torch.func.jacrev(model_fn_params_only, has_aux=True)(
        self.params_dict, self.buffers_dict
    )

    # Concatenate over flattened parameters
    Js = [
        j.flatten(start_dim=-p.dim())
        for j, p in zip(Js.values(), self.params_dict.values())
    ]
    Js = torch.cat(Js, dim=-1)

    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Js = Js[..., self.subnetwork_indices]

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute parameter Jacobians for selected output coordinates per input.

    The default computes all output Jacobians before selecting coordinates.
    Backends may override it to avoid materializing the full Jacobian.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        Input data on the model's device, with a leading batch dimension.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    # Use the output shape observed at this input. Reward models return two
    # training logits but one output for an individual inference input.
    jacobians, values = CurvatureInterface.jacobians(
        self, x, enable_backprop=enable_backprop
    )

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != jacobians.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    selected = torch.gather(
        jacobians,
        dim=1,
        index=outputs.to(jacobians.device, dtype=torch.long)
        .unsqueeze(-1)
        .expand(-1, -1, jacobians.shape[-1]),
    )

    return selected, values

def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute batch gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at
    current parameter \\(\\theta\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model. If
        MutableMapping, every tensor in it must have the batch as its first dim.
    y : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(batch * tokens, parameters)`, where `tokens` is the number
        of leading output dims per datum (1 if there are none)
    loss : torch.Tensor
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        # vmap only maps over tensors in plain containers, e.g. not `UserDict`.
        # The model then gets plain dicts, also for nested mappings; non-tensor
        # entries are passed as is. Tensors in nested containers are mapped over.
        def to_dict(x):
            if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
                return {k: to_dict(v) for k, v in x.items()}

            return x

        x = to_dict(x)
        in_dims_x = tree_map(lambda v: 0 if torch.is_tensor(v) else None, x)
    else:
        in_dims_x = 0

    def unsqueeze(x):
        return tree_map(lambda v: v.unsqueeze(0) if torch.is_tensor(v) else v, x)

    def loss_single(params_dict, buffers_dict, x, y):
        """Compute the loss of each token of a single sample."""
        x, y = unsqueeze(x), y.unsqueeze(0)  # vmap removes the batch dimension
        output = torch.func.functional_call(
            self.model, (params_dict, buffers_dict), x
        )
        self._check_targets(output, y)

        # Every leading dim of the output is a "token" with its own loss
        n_lead = output.ndim - 1
        output = output.flatten(end_dim=n_lead - 1)
        y = y.reshape(output.shape[0], *y.shape[n_lead:])

        def loss_token(output_t, y_t):
            return torch.func.functional_call(
                self.lossfunc, {}, (output_t.unsqueeze(0), y_t.unsqueeze(0))
            )

        losses = torch.func.vmap(loss_token)(output, y)
        return losses, losses.sum()

    jac_fn = torch.func.jacrev(loss_single, argnums=0, has_aux=True)
    batch_jac_fn = torch.func.vmap(jac_fn, in_dims=(None, None, in_dims_x, 0))

    try:
        batch_grad, batch_loss = batch_jac_fn(
            self.params_dict, self.buffers_dict, x, y
        )
    except RuntimeError as e:
        if "data-dependent control flow" not in str(e):
            raise

        raise ValueError(
            "Per-sample gradients for the empirical Fisher are computed with "
            + "`torch.func.vmap`, which does not support models with "
            + "data-dependent control flow (e.g. Huggingface transformers). "
            + "Consider using a GGN backend, e.g. `CurvlinopsGGN`, instead."
        ) from e

    # (batch * tokens, parameters)
    Gs = torch.cat([bg.flatten(start_dim=2) for bg in batch_grad.values()], dim=2)
    Gs = Gs.flatten(end_dim=1)

    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]

    loss = batch_loss.sum(0)

    return Gs, loss

def _loss(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute `self.lossfunc(f, y)`, where every leading dim of `f` but the last
    is a batch dim.

    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        # vmap only maps over tensors in plain containers, e.g. not `UserDict`.
        # The model then gets plain dicts, also for nested mappings; non-tensor
        # entries are passed as is. Tensors in nested containers are mapped over.
        def to_dict(x):
            if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
                return {k: to_dict(v) for k, v in x.items()}

            return x

        x = to_dict(x)
        in_dims_x = tree_map(lambda v: 0 if torch.is_tensor(v) else None, x)
    else:
        in_dims_x = 0

    def unsqueeze(x):
        return tree_map(lambda v: v.unsqueeze(0) if torch.is_tensor(v) else v, x)

    def loss_single(params_dict, buffers_dict, x, y):
        """Compute the loss of each token of a single sample."""
        x, y = unsqueeze(x), y.unsqueeze(0)  # vmap removes the batch dimension
        output = torch.func.functional_call(
            self.model, (params_dict, buffers_dict), x
        )
        self._check_targets(output, y)

        # Every leading dim of the output is a "token" with its own loss
        n_lead = output.ndim - 1
        output = output.flatten(end_dim=n_lead - 1)
        y = y.reshape(output.shape[0], *y.shape[n_lead:])

        def loss_token(output_t, y_t):
            return torch.func.functional_call(
                self.lossfunc, {}, (output_t.unsqueeze(0), y_t.unsqueeze(0))
            )

        losses = torch.func.vmap(loss_token)(output, y)
        return losses, losses.sum()

    jac_fn = torch.func.jacrev(loss_single, argnums=0, has_aux=True)
    batch_jac_fn = torch.func.vmap(jac_fn, in_dims=(None, None, in_dims_x, 0))

    try:
        batch_grad, batch_loss = batch_jac_fn(
            self.params_dict, self.buffers_dict, x, y
        )
    except RuntimeError as e:
        if "data-dependent control flow" not in str(e):
            raise

        raise ValueError(
            "Per-sample gradients for the empirical Fisher are computed with "
            + "`torch.func.vmap`, which does not support models with "
            + "data-dependent control flow (e.g. Huggingface transformers). "
            + "Consider using a GGN backend, e.g. `CurvlinopsGGN`, instead."
        ) from e

    # (batch * tokens, parameters)
    Gs = torch.cat([bg.flatten(start_dim=2) for bg in batch_grad.values()], dim=2)
    Gs = Gs.flatten(end_dim=1)

    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]

    loss = batch_loss.sum(0)

    return Gs, loss

_get_mc_functional_fisher(f: Tensor) -> Tensor

Approximate the Fisher's middle matrix (expected outer product of the functional gradient) using MC integral with self.num_samples many samples.

Source code in laplace/curvature/curvature.py 
def _get_mc_functional_fisher(self, f: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Approximate the Fisher's middle matrix (expected outer product of the functional gradient)
    using MC integral with `self.num_samples` many samples.
    """
    F = 0

    for _ in range(self.num_samples):
        if self.likelihood == "regression":
            # N(y | f, 1)
            y_sample = f + torch.randn(f.shape, device=f.device, dtype=f.dtype)
            grad_sample = f - y_sample  # functional MSE grad
        else:  # classification with softmax
            y_sample = torch.distributions.Multinomial(logits=f).sample()
            # First functional derivative of the loglik is p - y
            p = torch.softmax(f, dim=-1)
            grad_sample = p - y_sample

        F += (
            1
            / self.num_samples
            * torch.einsum("...c,...k->...ck", grad_sample, grad_sample)
        )

    return F

def _check_targets(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    """For classification, check that the targets `y` match the logits `f`
    `(batch, ..., classes)`: class indices `(batch, ...)` or class probabilities
    with the same shape as `f`.

    Flattening the batch dims would silently misalign targets of the wrong shape
    with the same number of elements, e.g. `(B, L, M)` instead of `(B, M, L)`.
    """
    if self.likelihood != Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION:
        return

    if y.shape != f.shape[:-1] and y.shape != f.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The targets have shape {tuple(y.shape)}, which matches neither the "
            f"class indices {tuple(f.shape[:-1])} nor the class probabilities "
            f"{tuple(f.shape)} expected from the logits."
        )

def _loss(self, f: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Compute `self.lossfunc(f, y)`, where every leading dim of `f` but the last
    is a batch dim.

    `CrossEntropyLoss` expects the class axis at dim 1, while Laplace puts it last,
    e.g. logits `(B, L, C)` with targets `(B, L)`. So, for classification, flatten
    the batch dims, which makes every token an observation.
    """
    self._check_targets(f, y)

    if self.likelihood == Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION and f.ndim > 2:
        # Class probabilities keep their class axis
        y = y.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1]) if y.ndim == f.ndim else y.reshape(-1)
        f = f.reshape(-1, f.shape[-1])

    return self.lossfunc(f, y)

def jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta} f(x;\\theta)\\) at current parameter \\(\\theta\\),
    via torch.func.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model.
    enable_backprop : bool, default = False
        whether to enable backprop through the Js and f w.r.t. x

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `([batch_dims], outputs, parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `([batch_dims], outputs)`
    """

    def model_fn_params_only(params_dict, buffers_dict):
        out = torch.func.functional_call(self.model, (params_dict, buffers_dict), x)
        return out, out

    Js, f = torch.func.jacrev(model_fn_params_only, has_aux=True)(
        self.params_dict, self.buffers_dict
    )

    # Concatenate over flattened parameters
    Js = [
        j.flatten(start_dim=-p.dim())
        for j, p in zip(Js.values(), self.params_dict.values())
    ]
    Js = torch.cat(Js, dim=-1)

    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Js = Js[..., self.subnetwork_indices]

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def last_layer_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute Jacobians \\(\\nabla_{\\theta_\\textrm{last}} f(x;\\theta_\\textrm{last})\\)
    only at current last-layer parameter \\(\\theta_{\\textrm{last}}\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Jacobians `(batch, outputs, last-layer-parameters)`
    f : torch.Tensor
        output function `(batch, outputs)`
    """
    f, phi = self.model.forward_with_features(x)
    if phi.ndim > 2:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Last-layer Laplace does not support inputs/outputs with more than "
            "one batch dimension (e.g. sequences) yet."
        )
    bsize = phi.shape[0]
    output_size = int(f.numel() / bsize)

    # calculate Jacobians using the feature vector 'phi'
    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute parameter Jacobians for selected output coordinates per input.

    The default computes all output Jacobians before selecting coordinates.
    Backends may override it to avoid materializing the full Jacobian.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        Input data on the model's device, with a leading batch dimension.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    # Use the output shape observed at this input. Reward models return two
    # training logits but one output for an individual inference input.
    jacobians, values = CurvatureInterface.jacobians(
        self, x, enable_backprop=enable_backprop
    )

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != jacobians.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    selected = torch.gather(
        jacobians,
        dim=1,
        index=outputs.to(jacobians.device, dtype=torch.long)
        .unsqueeze(-1)
        .expand(-1, -1, jacobians.shape[-1]),
    )

    return selected, values

        of leading output dims per datum (1 if there are none)

        y = y.reshape(output.shape[0], *y.shape[n_lead:])

        def loss_token(output_t, y_t):
            return torch.func.functional_call(
                self.lossfunc, {}, (output_t.unsqueeze(0), y_t.unsqueeze(0))
            )

        losses = torch.func.vmap(loss_token)(output, y)
        return losses, losses.sum()

    batch_jac_fn = torch.func.vmap(jac_fn, in_dims=(None, None, in_dims_x, 0))

            self.params_dict, self.buffers_dict, x, y

    p = next(self.model.parameters())
    identity = (
        torch.eye(output_size, device=p.device, dtype=p.dtype)
        .unsqueeze(0)
        .tile(bsize, 1, 1)
    )
    # Jacobians are batch x output x params
    Js = torch.einsum("kp,kij->kijp", phi, identity).reshape(bsize, output_size, -1)
    if self.model.last_layer.bias is not None:
        Js = torch.cat([Js, identity], dim=2)

    return (Js, f) if enable_backprop else (Js.detach(), f.detach())

def selected_output_jacobians(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any],
    outputs: torch.Tensor,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute parameter Jacobians for selected output coordinates per input.

    The default computes all output Jacobians before selecting coordinates.
    Backends may override it to avoid materializing the full Jacobian.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        Input data on the model's device, with a leading batch dimension.
    outputs : torch.Tensor
        Output indices for each input, shaped `(batch,)` or
        `(batch, selected_outputs)`.
    enable_backprop : bool, default=False
        Whether to retain gradients through the Jacobians and model outputs.

    Returns
    -------
    Js : torch.Tensor
        Selected Jacobians of shape `(batch, selected_outputs, parameters)`.
    f : torch.Tensor
        Model outputs of shape `(batch, outputs)`.
    """
    # Use the output shape observed at this input. Reward models return two
    # training logits but one output for an individual inference input.
    jacobians, values = CurvatureInterface.jacobians(
        self, x, enable_backprop=enable_backprop
    )

    if outputs.ndim == 1:
        outputs = outputs[:, None]

    if outputs.shape[0] != jacobians.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("Output selectors must match the input batch size.")

    selected = torch.gather(
        jacobians,
        dim=1,
        index=outputs.to(jacobians.device, dtype=torch.long)
        .unsqueeze(-1)
        .expand(-1, -1, jacobians.shape[-1]),
    )

    return selected, values

def gradients(
    self, x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping[str, torch.Tensor | Any], y: torch.Tensor
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute batch gradients \\(\\nabla_\\theta \\ell(f(x;\\theta, y)\\) at
    current parameter \\(\\theta\\).

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        input data `(batch, input_shape)` on compatible device with model. If
        MutableMapping, every tensor in it must have the batch as its first dim.
    y : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    Gs : torch.Tensor
        gradients `(batch * tokens, parameters)`, where `tokens` is the number
        of leading output dims per datum (1 if there are none)
    loss : torch.Tensor
    """
    if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
        # vmap only maps over tensors in plain containers, e.g. not `UserDict`.
        # The model then gets plain dicts, also for nested mappings; non-tensor
        # entries are passed as is. Tensors in nested containers are mapped over.
        def to_dict(x):
            if isinstance(x, MutableMapping):
                return {k: to_dict(v) for k, v in x.items()}

            return x

        x = to_dict(x)
        in_dims_x = tree_map(lambda v: 0 if torch.is_tensor(v) else None, x)
    else:
        in_dims_x = 0

    def unsqueeze(x):
        return tree_map(lambda v: v.unsqueeze(0) if torch.is_tensor(v) else v, x)

    def loss_single(params_dict, buffers_dict, x, y):
        """Compute the loss of each token of a single sample."""
        x, y = unsqueeze(x), y.unsqueeze(0)  # vmap removes the batch dimension
        output = torch.func.functional_call(
            self.model, (params_dict, buffers_dict), x
        )
        self._check_targets(output, y)

        # Every leading dim of the output is a "token" with its own loss
        n_lead = output.ndim - 1
        output = output.flatten(end_dim=n_lead - 1)
        y = y.reshape(output.shape[0], *y.shape[n_lead:])

        def loss_token(output_t, y_t):
            return torch.func.functional_call(
                self.lossfunc, {}, (output_t.unsqueeze(0), y_t.unsqueeze(0))
            )

        losses = torch.func.vmap(loss_token)(output, y)
        return losses, losses.sum()

    jac_fn = torch.func.jacrev(loss_single, argnums=0, has_aux=True)
    batch_jac_fn = torch.func.vmap(jac_fn, in_dims=(None, None, in_dims_x, 0))

    try:
        batch_grad, batch_loss = batch_jac_fn(
            self.params_dict, self.buffers_dict, x, y
        )
    except RuntimeError as e:
        if "data-dependent control flow" not in str(e):
            raise

        raise ValueError(
            "Per-sample gradients for the empirical Fisher are computed with "
            + "`torch.func.vmap`, which does not support models with "
            + "data-dependent control flow (e.g. Huggingface transformers). "
            + "Consider using a GGN backend, e.g. `CurvlinopsGGN`, instead."
        ) from e

    # (batch * tokens, parameters)
    Gs = torch.cat([bg.flatten(start_dim=2) for bg in batch_grad.values()], dim=2)
    Gs = Gs.flatten(end_dim=1)

    if self.subnetwork_indices is not None:
        Gs = Gs[:, self.subnetwork_indices]

    loss = batch_loss.sum(0)

    return Gs, loss

Bases: BaseFunctionalLaplace

Accelerated linearized Laplace using a rank-limited Nyström feature map.

The pretrained model stays fixed. Fitting selects a subset of training inputs, builds parameter-Jacobian features, and accumulates projected GGN curvature. A numerically rank-deficient subset cannot supply the requested number of features.

Parameters:

  • model (Module) –

    Pretrained network to linearize.

  • likelihood (Likelihood or str) –

    "classification", "regression", or "reward_modeling".

  • subsample_size (int) –

    Number of training inputs used to construct the Nyström basis.

  • n_eigenvalues (int) –

    Number of positive kernel directions retained, at most subsample_size.

  • sigma_noise (float or Tensor, default: 1.0 ) –

    Observation standard deviation for regression.

  • prior_precision (float or Tensor, default: 1.0 ) –

    Scalar parameter-prior precision.

  • prior_mean (float or Tensor, default: 0.0 ) –

    Prior mean; only zero is supported.

  • temperature (float, default: 1.0 ) –

    Positive scale of the likelihood curvature.

  • enable_backprop (bool, default: False ) –

    Retain derivatives through predictive moments.

  • dict_key_x (str, default: "input_ids" ) –

    Input key for mapping-style batches.

  • dict_key_y (str, default: "labels" ) –

    Target key for mapping-style batches.

  • backend (type[CurvatureInterface] or None, default: None ) –

    Curvature backend used to compute parameter Jacobians.

  • backend_kwargs (dict[str, Any] or None, default: None ) –

    Additional curvature backend options.

  • seed (int, default: 1234 ) –

    Seed for selecting basis inputs and output coordinates.

Attributes:

  • fit_history_ (dict[str, list[Any]]) –

    processed_examples records cumulative curvature-pass counts, val_nll records validation scores, and tuning records candidate hyperparameters and their validation scores.

  • dual_directions (Tensor or None) –

    Fitted parameter-space basis shaped [parameters, n_eigenvalues].

  • feature_gram (Tensor or None) –

    Accumulated projected curvature shaped [n_eigenvalues, n_eigenvalues] before noise and temperature scaling.

  • chol_precision (Tensor or None) –

    Lower Cholesky factor of the feature-space posterior precision.

Notes

fit returns None. fit_history_ stores processed example counts, validation NLL, and prior-grid scores when those options are used.

def __init__(
    self,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    likelihood: Likelihood | str,
    subsample_size: int,
    n_eigenvalues: int,
    sigma_noise: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_precision: float | torch.Tensor = 1.0,
    prior_mean: float | torch.Tensor = 0.0,
    temperature: float = 1.0,
    enable_backprop: bool = False,
    dict_key_x: str = "input_ids",
    dict_key_y: str = "labels",
    backend: type[CurvatureInterface] | None = None,
    backend_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    seed: int = 1234,
) -> None:
    """Initialize ELLA from the pretrained model and basis configuration."""
    if (
        not isinstance(subsample_size, Integral)
        or isinstance(subsample_size, bool)
        or not isinstance(n_eigenvalues, Integral)
        or isinstance(n_eigenvalues, bool)
        or subsample_size <= 0
        or n_eigenvalues <= 0
        or n_eigenvalues > subsample_size
    ):
        raise ValueError("Require 0 < n_eigenvalues <= subsample_size.")
    if torch.as_tensor(prior_precision).numel() != 1:
        raise ValueError("ELLA requires scalar prior_precision.")
    if torch.any(torch.as_tensor(prior_mean) != 0):
        raise ValueError("ELLA currently requires prior_mean=0.")
    if not isfinite(temperature) or temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError("temperature must be positive and finite.")
    super().__init__(
        model,
        likelihood,
        sigma_noise=sigma_noise,
        prior_precision=prior_precision,
        prior_mean=prior_mean,
        temperature=temperature,
        enable_backprop=enable_backprop,
        dict_key_x=dict_key_x,
        dict_key_y=dict_key_y,
        backend=backend,
        backend_kwargs=backend_kwargs,
    )
    self.subsample_size = subsample_size
    self.n_eigenvalues = n_eigenvalues
    self.seed = seed
    self.dual_directions: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self.feature_gram: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self.chol_precision: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._posterior_dirty = False
    self._fitted = False
    self.fit_history_: dict[str, list[Any]] = {
        "processed_examples": [],
        "val_nll": [],
        "tuning": [],
    }

Predict from the fitted function-space posterior.

Parameters:

  • x (Tensor or MutableMapping) –

    Batched model inputs.

  • pred_type (PredType or str, default: PredType.GP ) –

    Prediction type. Function-space estimators support only "gp".

  • joint (bool, default: False ) –

    Retain cross-input covariance for regression predictions.

  • link_approx (LinkApprox or str, default: LinkApprox.PROBIT ) –

    Approximation for the classification probability link.

  • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

    Number of draws for a Monte Carlo classification link.

  • diagonal_output (bool, default: False ) –

    Return only output variances for regression when supported.

  • generator (Generator or None, default: None ) –

    Random generator for Monte Carlo classification predictions.

  • fitting (bool, default: False ) –

    Evaluate reward-model preference pairs as classification inputs.

  • **model_kwargs (Any, default: {} ) –

    Accepted for compatibility with the base prediction interface; these arguments are not forwarded to the model.

Returns:

  • Tensor or tuple[Tensor, Tensor] –

    Classification probabilities [B, C], or regression/reward latent mean and covariance. With joint=True, the regression mean is flattened and covariance has shape [B*O, B*O].

Raises:

  • RuntimeError –

    If the posterior has not been fitted.

  • ValueError –

    If the input batch is empty, the prediction type or link is unsupported, or the generator has an incompatible type or device.

Warns:

  • RuntimeWarning –

    For "bridge" and "bridge_norm" when gradient tracking is enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal, nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive normal value of the covariance dtype.

Notes

Regression and individual reward predictions exclude observation noise. Their marginal mean is [B, O] and covariance is [B, O, O], or variance [B, O] with diagonal_output=True.

The "bridge" and "bridge_norm" links use float64 intermediate calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype. Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to avoid overflow. If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses the probit approximation on centered moments before variance normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite. Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.

def __call__(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    pred_type: PredType | str = PredType.GP,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
    generator: torch.Generator | None = None,
    fitting: bool = False,
    **model_kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Predict from the fitted function-space posterior.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        Batched model inputs.
    pred_type : PredType or str, default=PredType.GP
        Prediction type. Function-space estimators support only ``"gp"``.
    joint : bool, default=False
        Retain cross-input covariance for regression predictions.
    link_approx : LinkApprox or str, default=LinkApprox.PROBIT
        Approximation for the classification probability link.
    n_samples : int, default=100
        Number of draws for a Monte Carlo classification link.
    diagonal_output : bool, default=False
        Return only output variances for regression when supported.
    generator : torch.Generator or None, default=None
        Random generator for Monte Carlo classification predictions.
    fitting : bool, default=False
        Evaluate reward-model preference pairs as classification inputs.
    **model_kwargs : Any
        Accepted for compatibility with the base prediction interface;
        these arguments are not forwarded to the model.

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor or tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
        Classification probabilities ``[B, C]``, or regression/reward
        latent mean and covariance. With ``joint=True``, the regression
        mean is flattened and covariance has shape ``[B*O, B*O]``.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        If the posterior has not been fitted.
    ValueError
        If the input batch is empty, the prediction type or link is
        unsupported, or the generator has an incompatible type or device.

    Warns
    -----
    RuntimeWarning
        For ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` when gradient tracking is
        enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal,
        nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest
        absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive
        normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    Regression and individual reward predictions exclude observation
    noise. Their marginal mean is ``[B, O]`` and covariance is
    ``[B, O, O]``, or variance ``[B, O]`` with ``diagonal_output=True``.

    The ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` links use float64 intermediate
    calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype.
    Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to
    avoid overflow.
    If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are
    nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses
    the probit approximation on centered moments before variance
    normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can
    exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients
    may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite.
    Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A
    RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.
    """
    self._check_fitted()
    self._check_nonempty_inputs(x)
    if pred_type != PredType.GP:
        raise ValueError("Only gp is supported as a functional prediction type.")
    if link_approx not in list(LinkApprox):
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported link approximation {link_approx}.")
    if generator is not None and (
        not isinstance(generator, torch.Generator)
        or generator.device != self._device
    ):
        raise ValueError("Invalid random generator (check type and device).")
    likelihood = self.likelihood
    if likelihood == Likelihood.REWARD_MODELING:
        likelihood = Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION if fitting else Likelihood.REGRESSION
    if likelihood == Likelihood.CLASSIFICATION and link_approx == LinkApprox.MC:
        return self.predictive_samples(
            x,
            n_samples=n_samples,
            diagonal_output=diagonal_output,
            generator=generator,
            fitting=fitting,
        ).mean(dim=0)
    return self._glm_forward_call(
        x, likelihood, joint, link_approx, n_samples, diagonal_output
    )

def _gridsearch(
    self,
    loss: torchmetrics.Metric
    | Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor]
    | Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
    interval: torch.Tensor,
    val_loader: DataLoader,
    pred_type: PredType | str,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    progress_bar: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    assert callable(loss) or isinstance(loss, torchmetrics.Metric)

    results: list[float] = list()
    prior_precs: list[torch.Tensor] = list()
    pbar = tqdm.tqdm(interval, disable=not progress_bar)

    for prior_prec in pbar:
        self.prior_precision = prior_prec

        try:
            result = validate(
                self,
                val_loader,
                loss,
                pred_type=pred_type,
                link_approx=link_approx,
                n_samples=n_samples,
                dict_key_y=self.dict_key_y,
            )
        except LinAlgError:
            result = np.inf
        except RuntimeError as err:
            if "not positive definite" in str(err):
                result = np.inf
            else:
                raise err

        if progress_bar:
            pbar.set_description(
                f"[Grid search | prior_prec: {prior_prec:.3e}, loss: {result:.3f}]"
            )

        results.append(result)
        prior_precs.append(prior_prec)

    return prior_precs[np.argmin(results)]

Compute the posterior predictive on input data x for "glm" pred type.

Parameters:

  • x (Tensor or MutableMapping) –

    (batch_size, input_shape) if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain the said tensor.

  • likelihood (Likelihood or str in {'classification', 'regression', 'reward_modeling'}) –

    determines the log likelihood Hessian approximation.

  • link_approx (('mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'), default: 'mc' ) –

    how to approximate the classification link function for the 'glm'. For pred_type='nn', only 'mc' is possible.

  • joint (bool, default: False ) –

    Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with pred_type='glm'. If set to True, the predictive distribution has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]). If False, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution. Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

  • n_samples (int, default: 100 ) –

    number of samples for link_approx='mc'.

  • diagonal_output (bool, default: False ) –

    whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs. Only works for pred_type='glm' and link_approx='mc'.

Returns:

  • predictive ( Tensor or tuple[Tensor] ) –

    For likelihood='classification', a torch.Tensor is returned with a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape as the logits, e.g. (batch, classes) or (batch, seq_len, classes). For likelihood='regression', a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive variance. For likelihood='regression' and joint=True, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance.

Warns:

  • RuntimeWarning –

    For "bridge" and "bridge_norm" when gradient tracking is enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal, nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive normal value of the covariance dtype.

Notes

The "bridge" and "bridge_norm" links use float64 intermediate calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype. Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to avoid overflow. If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses the probit approximation on centered moments before variance normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite. Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.

def _glm_forward_call(
    self,
    x: torch.Tensor | MutableMapping,
    likelihood: Likelihood | str,
    joint: bool = False,
    link_approx: LinkApprox | str = LinkApprox.PROBIT,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    diagonal_output: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute the posterior predictive on input data `x` for "glm" pred type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : torch.Tensor or MutableMapping
        `(batch_size, input_shape)` if tensor. If MutableMapping, must contain
        the said tensor.

    likelihood : Likelihood or str in {'classification', 'regression', 'reward_modeling'}
        determines the log likelihood Hessian approximation.

    link_approx : {'mc', 'probit', 'bridge', 'bridge_norm'}
        how to approximate the classification link function for the `'glm'`.
        For `pred_type='nn'`, only 'mc' is possible.

    joint : bool
        Whether to output a joint predictive distribution in regression with
        `pred_type='glm'`. If set to `True`, the predictive distribution
        has the same form as GP posterior, i.e. N([f(x1), ...,f(xm)], Cov[f(x1), ..., f(xm)]).
        If `False`, then only outputs the marginal predictive distribution.
        Only available for regression and GLM predictive.

    n_samples : int
        number of samples for `link_approx='mc'`.

    diagonal_output : bool
        whether to use a diagonalized posterior predictive on the outputs.
        Only works for `pred_type='glm'` and `link_approx='mc'`.

    Returns
    -------
    predictive: torch.Tensor or tuple[torch.Tensor]
        For `likelihood='classification'`, a torch.Tensor is returned with
        a distribution over classes (similar to a Softmax), with the same shape
        as the logits, e.g. `(batch, classes)` or `(batch, seq_len, classes)`.
        For `likelihood='regression'`, a tuple of torch.Tensor is returned
        with the mean and the predictive variance.
        For `likelihood='regression'` and `joint=True`, a tuple of torch.Tensor
        is returned with the mean and the predictive covariance.

    Warns
    -----
    RuntimeWarning
        For ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` when gradient tracking is
        enabled and a covariance requiring gradients has subnormal,
        nonzero magnitude for an input row. Magnitude is the largest
        absolute covariance entry, compared with the smallest positive
        normal value of the covariance dtype.

    Notes
    -----
    The ``"bridge"`` and ``"bridge_norm"`` links use float64 intermediate
    calculations and return probabilities in the predictive mean's dtype.
    Mean corrections and normalization use scaled logit differences to
    avoid overflow.
    If corrected variances or the optional normalization scale are
    nonpositive, or the Bridge probabilities are nonfinite, prediction uses
    the probit approximation on centered moments before variance
    normalization. Corrected variances are clamped at zero for this fallback.

    For subnormal covariance magnitudes, covariance-entry derivatives can
    exceed their dtype's range. Covariance or upstream parameter gradients
    may therefore contain inf or NaN even when probabilities remain finite.
    Covariance backpropagation is not reliable in this regime. A
    RuntimeWarning is emitted when covariance gradients are tracked.
    """
    f_mu, f_var = self._glm_predictive_distribution(
        x, joint=joint and likelihood == Likelihood.REGRESSION
    )

    if likelihood == Likelihood.REGRESSION:
        if diagonal_output and not joint:
            f_var = torch.diagonal(f_var, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)
        return f_mu, f_var

    # Every leading dim of the logits but the last is a batch dim, e.g. `(B, L, C)`
    # for sequences. The link approximations work on `(N, C)`, so flatten them.
    batch_shape = f_mu.shape[:-1]
    f_mu = f_mu.reshape(-1, f_mu.shape[-1])
    f_var = f_var.reshape(-1, *f_var.shape[-2:])

    probs = self._glm_classification_link(
        f_mu, f_var, link_approx, n_samples, diagonal_output
    )
    return probs.reshape(*batch_shape, probs.shape[-1])
